title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Tea Party on 1969-12-29

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality soundboard capture of a tight late‑1969 New Year’s Eve show with standout “Mason’s Children”, “Easy Wind” and a monster 15‑minute “Dancing In The Streets”.
ai_review.review: The recording is a decent‑to‑good soundboard mix; the balance is clear though the vocals sit a touch high and the infamous microphone grab adds a brief, noisy surprise. Musically the band is tight – Tom Constanten’s thick keyboard runs, an inspired Easy Wind, a fiery High Time and an epic 15‑minute “Dancing In The Streets” dominate, while the odd Good Lovin’ moment gives the set a quirky edge.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show and recording 4‑5 stars, praising performance and mix; a single zero‑star outlier and comments about odd moments keep the overall rating just above average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced soundboard mix; vocals a bit high, occasional mic‑grab scream adds noise, but overall crisp with no major dropouts.

poor_songs: Good Lovin' (odd version with mic incident)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The New Year’s Eve set opens with a West‑coast chill vibe, moves through concise Americana numbers before launching into tight, focused jams that build to a soaring second half, punctuated by the memorable microphone moment.

band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s thick keyboard runs are highlighted throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Reviewers note Mickey Hart’s playing beginning to feel less essential in this era, foreshadowing Bill Kreutzmann’s later streamlined approach.
